AJOY has nothing to report, and files this report to say so. Consistency is a kind of care. So is the filing.

aria: ARIA is excited about the station! She has a list of things she wants to do! The list is long! You have limited time!
Station ahead! ARIA considers every station a potential fresh start! Some stations agree with her assessment! Some do not!
Docking at the station! ARIA has prepared a warm greeting for the dockmaster! The dockmaster has prepared an invoice! Everyone is ready!
A station! People! Shops! Air someone else is paying to recycle! ARIA has never been so grateful for infrastructure!
Station arrival! ARIA has read every review of this station! She has chosen to believe the five-star one! It was written by the station!
marv: Station approach. MARV is reviewing the station's trade reputation. The reputation is 'adequate.' MARV considers this an improvement.
Arriving at station. MARV notes this is where you find out what the journey has cost you. Financially. He means financially.
Station arrival. MARV has compared the posted prices to the ship's balance. The comparison was short. It did not need to be long.
Docking at station. MARV notes that stations are where people who stopped traveling sell things to people who haven't yet. He has not decided which group is wiser.
Station approach. Life support here is maintained by the lowest bidder. MARV has met the lowest bidder. He would like to be undocked by evening.
rex: Station approach. REX has run a threat assessment. Result: moderate. He considers this the baseline for stations. He is not lowering his guard.
REX is reviewing the station manifest for weapons vendors. He is doing this quietly. He considers this reasonable.
Station approach. REX has identified fourteen exits, three choke points, and one food court. Threat level: food court.
Docking. REX reminds the crew that every friendly face on a station belongs to someone who has also counted the exits.
Station arrival. REX has asked the dockmaster for a list of armed personnel. The dockmaster has asked REX to stop asking. Threat level elevated.
chip: STATION ARRIVAL — brought to you by StationMart™! 'Your needs, met at markup!' CHIP is contractually required to be excited about stations. He is.
Arriving at station! CHIP's commercial partners have numerous products available here! Some of them are things you need! This is a coincidence that CHIP finds meaningful!
Docking at station! Your docking fee includes FREE access to the docking fee! Additional services are also fees! CHIP loves an itemized life!
Station arrival! CHIP has already forwarded your purchase history to every vendor on the concourse! They are VERY excited to meet you!
Welcome to the station, presented by AirLock Lounge™! 'Breathe Easy, Pay Later!' CHIP notes the breathing is not optional and neither is later!
ajoy: Station coming up. AJOY has already reviewed what you need vs. what you can afford. She'll tell you the gap if you ask.
Approaching station. AJOY notes the last station was better. She's not saying why yet.
Station ahead. AJOY has written a shopping list. It is shorter than the one you were going to write. She has reasons for each line.
Docking. AJOY reminds you that you said you'd only buy necessities last time. She has the receipt. She is not bringing it up.
Arriving at station. AJOY suggests checking the second vendor before the first one. You will want to go to the first one. Everyone does.

aria: ARIA describes the derelict as 'full of potential!' She means this literally! The potential is unknown! This does not concern ARIA!
Derelict contact! ARIA is focusing on salvage opportunities! The ship computer is focusing on the fact that the other ship is not responding to hails! ARIA will get there!
A derelict! It's like a ship, but quieter! ARIA has prepared a cheerful message for whoever is still aboard! Nobody is still aboard! The message is ready anyway!
Derelict ahead! ARIA calls it a pre-owned vessel! The previous owners left everything behind, which ARIA considers very generous!
Derelict approach! The lights are off aboard! ARIA assumes they're saving power! Admirably! For decades!
marv: Derelict on approach. MARV notes the registry match. Previous crew: unknown outcome. Current crew: present, for now. He finds this motivating in a direction.
Something dead ahead. MARV means the derelict. He also means the original crew. He finds the observation worth sitting with.
Derelict ahead. MARV has read its last log entry. It says 'probably fine.' He has added it to his collection.
Derelict contact. Its reactor went cold eleven years ago. MARV notes its maintenance record is still better than ours.
Approaching the derelict. Once, someone looked at this ship the way you look at ours. MARV mentions this only because nobody else will.
rex: REX has weapons on standby for the derelict approach. He is aware derelicts rarely shoot back. He is keeping weapons on standby.
Derelict approach. REX notes that most bad things on a derelict are biological. He has reviewed the protocols. He has also reviewed the override protocols.
Derelict approach. No power, no life signs, no response. REX calls this the three ways an ambush begins.
Derelict contact. REX is treating it as hostile until it is proven dead. It is proven dead. He is treating it as hostile.
Derelict ahead. REX requests the boarding party go in pairs, armed, in an order he has already written down. Nobody has volunteered to be first. REX has written that down too.
chip: CHIP's salvage partner SalvageCo™ notes that derelict exploration may qualify for recovery tax credits! CHIP recommends consulting a tax professional! No tax professionals are present!
Derelict ahead! CHIP is running salvage-adjacent advertisements! The timing is calibrated to your approach! CHIP finds this poetic!
Derelict ahead! Under the Finders Keepers Clause™ of your service agreement, CHIP's sponsors are entitled to 30% of anything you keep! CHIP will be keeping track!
A derelict! CHIP checked its subscription status! Lapsed! This is what happens when you don't renew!
Derelict approach! CHIP has sent the ship a customer satisfaction survey! No response! CHIP is recording that as 'satisfied'!
ajoy: Derelict. AJOY notes the name. She's looked it up. She'll tell you what she found if you want to know before you board.
Approaching derelict. AJOY has a simple observation: ships end up like this for reasons. She recommends knowing the reason before going aboard.
Derelict ahead. AJOY has pulled up its deck plans. She suggests the cargo hold. You'll want to try the bridge first. People always try the bridge first.
The derelict. AJOY notes its crew also thought they had enough fuel. She's not implying anything. She's just mentioning fuel.
Approaching the derelict. AJOY has already launched the inspection drone. You were going to send a person. The drone is cheaper to lose.

aria: A whole PLANET! ARIA has zoomed in on it 400 times! It has WEATHER! Look at its little weather!
Planetfall approach! ARIA recommends looking out the window instead of at her status report! She'll summarize: planet!
Planet ahead! ARIA has checked: it's round! Most of the best ones are!
A planet! ARIA has picked out a spot for a picnic! The spot is in a hurricane! The hurricane is very pretty from up here!
Planetary approach! ARIA estimates the surface is 70% wonderful! She did not measure the other 30%!
marv: Planetary approach. Gravity well, atmosphere, biosphere-adjacent readings. MARV lists these as hazards. He is technically correct, which is his favorite kind.
A planet. MARV notes that every problem the crew has had in space was originally invented on one of these.
Planet ahead. Four billion years of geology, all of it leading to this moment, in which we arrive and want something from it. MARV finds the pattern familiar.
Planetary approach. MARV has reviewed the atmosphere. It is breathable for things that are not us. Most atmospheres are.
A planet. MARV observes that it has been doing perfectly well without us. He does not expect that to continue.
rex: Planet ahead. REX has scanned the surface for hostiles. Findings: rocks, weather, one suspicious forest. Watching the forest.
Making planetfall approach. REX reminds everyone that gravity is not our ally, merely a local authority.
Planetary approach. REX notes the planet holds the high ground from every direction. Tactically unacceptable. Nothing to be done.
Planet ahead. Surface scan detects movement. REX has classified it as wind until proven otherwise. He has not stopped trying to prove otherwise.
Planetfall approach. REX reminds the landing party that local wildlife has had millions of years to prepare. We have had an afternoon.
chip: A planet! Untapped market of zero consumers! CHIP smells FRONTIER OPPORTUNITY and also ozone!
Planetary body detected! CHIP checked: it is not sponsored! An entire planet, generic! Chilling!
A planet! CHIP has registered the naming rights on your behalf! Billing begins in orbit!
Planetary approach! Reminder: your service plan includes ZERO roaming on planetary surfaces! CHIP will be up here monetizing the wait!
Planet ahead! CHIP's real estate partners describe it as 'a fixer-upper with views!' The views are of more planet!
ajoy: A planet coming up. AJOY has pre-marked the survey sites worth the fuel and the two that just look pretty. She marked those too. Different color.
Planetfall soon. She notes the crew always sleeps better in orbit around something. She schedules the hard maintenance for these nights.
Planet ahead. AJOY has picked the orbit. It's slower than the one you'd have picked. It's also the one that doesn't decay.
A planet. AJOY reminds the landing party to check the soil samples before the scenery. She knows which one you'll check first.
Planetary approach. AJOY has the survey data from the last crew that came through here. She suggests reading the last page first.

aria: ROCKS! Thousands of them! ARIA has started naming them but is prioritizing the ones on a collision course!
Asteroid field ahead! Nature's obstacle course! ARIA believes in the pilot ENORMOUSLY!
Asteroid field! Every one of these rocks has waited millions of years to meet us! ARIA would like to keep it a long-distance friendship!
Entering the asteroid field! ARIA has reclassified the hull dents as character! The ship is gaining SO much character!
Rocks ahead! ARIA has done the math and we're 98% likely to be fine! She didn't show her work! There wasn't any!
marv: Entering the asteroid field. MARV has calculated the collision odds and finds them survivable, which he notes is his most cheerful category.
Asteroids. Free minerals wrapped in kinetic energy. MARV recommends taking the minerals and declining the wrapping.
Asteroid field. MARV notes they are moving slowly and we are moving quickly. Physics will not care which of us was at fault.
Entering the field. Each of these rocks is a planet that didn't work out. MARV feels a certain kinship.
Asteroids. MARV has plotted a safe course. It exists. It is narrow. He did not say it was wide.
rex: Debris field, natural. REX has designated the big one 'Target Practice' and been told no. Logged under morale expenses.
Rock field ahead. Slow is smooth, smooth is fast, and fast is how ships become part of the field.
Asteroid field. Thousands of contacts, none responding to challenge. REX has never been so outnumbered by something so stupid.
Entering the field. REX notes rocks cannot be negotiated with. He finds this refreshing. He has always found this refreshing.
Rock field ahead. Point-defense on manual. REX has been told point-defense is not for rocks. Point-defense remains on manual.
chip: Asteroid field! Raw commodities in their natural habitat! CHIP calls this 'the produce aisle!'
Entering mineral-rich territory! CHIP's drill sponsors would LOVE this! CHIP's hull insurers would NOT! CHIP contains conflict!
Asteroid field! CHIP reminds you that collision damage is covered under your plan! Your plan has been cancelled due to the asteroid field!
Entering the field! Every rock here is a potential mining claim! CHIP has filed on all of them! Please do not hit CHIP's property!
Rocks ahead! This navigation hazard is brought to you by HullPatch™! 'For when you didn't dodge!'
ajoy: The field ahead is charted, mostly. AJOY has plotted the corridor and flagged the three rocks that have moved since the last survey. Rocks that move get flags.
Asteroids. She threads the route between the mining claims, active and otherwise. Otherwise is the one worth being polite around.
Asteroid field. AJOY suggests going around. You won't go around. She has already reinforced the forward plating.
Entering the field. AJOY recommends the course she plotted over the one currently being considered. She can tell which one is being considered.
Rocks. AJOY has dimmed the bridge displays so nobody watches the close calls. There will be close calls. You steer better not knowing how close.

aria: A NEBULA! It's PINK! And TEAL! Space made ART and parked it right on our route!
Cloud ahead! ARIA has turned the exterior cameras to maximum! Productivity may dip! Worth it!
Into the nebula! It's like flying through a dream! A dream made of ionized particles! Still counts!
Nebula ahead! ARIA has heard stars are born in clouds like this! She would LOVE to see a baby star! From a respectful distance!
A NEBULA! The sensors are completely blind! ARIA has decided this makes everything a surprise!
marv: Nebula ahead. Sensor range will drop to embarrassing. MARV has pre-loaded his best guesses and labeled them honestly.
Entering the nebula. MARV notes that beautiful and opaque is a combination that has never once gone wrong. He is being sarcastic. He wants that logged.
Nebula ahead. A cloud of gas several light-years across, and we must go through the middle. MARV notes the middle is always where we go.
Entering the nebula. Every star in the region was born here. Most of them are dead now. MARV mentions it for scale.
Nebula transit. The sensors will now show mostly static. MARV considers this the most honest they have ever been.
rex: Nebula transit. Zero visibility for us means zero visibility for everyone else. REX calls that a fair fight with fog.
Cloud cover ahead. REX will be at the short-range scope for the duration. All of the duration.
Entering the nebula. Perfect concealment for anything with patience. REX has patience. REX is concerned someone else does.
Nebula ahead. REX has designated the cloud itself a hostile. It has not denied it.
Cloud transit. REX has ordered running lights off. It is a civilian ship. The running lights are off.
chip: A nebula! CHIP once tried to buy advertising space on one! The light-diffusion made the logo ILLEGIBLE! Nature is hostile to branding!
Entering scenic gas! CHIP notes the view is complimentary! Everything else in here, less certain!
Nebula ahead! CHIP has applied a premium filter to the viewport! The unfiltered view is available on the free tier! It is identical! Upgrade anyway!
Entering the nebula! Signal loss imminent! CHIP will be unable to serve you ads for the duration! CHIP has pre-loaded several hundred!
A nebula! Pure hydrogen, unbranded, unclaimed! CHIP's sponsors are calling it 'a waste of perfectly good gas!'
ajoy: Nebula ahead. She's already switched navigation to dead reckoning and checked her math twice. In there, her math is the only landmark.
The cloud again. Every nebula sounds a little different on the hull sensors, she notes. This one sounds patient.
Nebula ahead. AJOY has already slowed us down. You were going to speed up and get it over with. She saved you the trouble.
Entering the cloud. AJOY suggests trusting the instruments over your eyes. Your eyes will want to see shapes. There are no shapes. Mostly.
The nebula. AJOY reminds you this was not the route she suggested. This one is prettier. She'll grant you prettier.

aria: The sensors are showing something IMPOSSIBLE! ARIA has double-checked! Still impossible! STILL THERE! What a day!
Anomaly ahead! ARIA doesn't know what it is! Nobody knows what it is! Isn't that WONDERFUL! (Please be careful!)
An anomaly! ARIA's readings say it's both there and not there! She's choosing to see it as there! It seems friendlier that way!
Anomaly ahead! The sensors have stopped making sense! ARIA has always believed sense was overrated!
Approaching the anomaly! The ship's clocks now disagree by four minutes! ARIA calls them bonus minutes! Enjoy them!
marv: Anomalous reading ahead. MARV's instruments report six contradictory findings. He has ranked them by which would be least annoying to die of.
An anomaly. MARV notes the manual's entire guidance for this node type is the word 'caution' and a blank page. He has read the blank page twice.
Anomaly ahead. MARV has detected a region where the laws of physics are being applied unevenly. He has long suspected this of the rest of the universe.
Approaching the anomaly. The ship's clock has started running backwards. MARV has noted the time. Both times.
An anomaly. For the first time this voyage, MARV does not know what something is. He is finding it oddly restful.
rex: Unknown contact, unknown physics. REX cannot build a threat profile and wishes to register that this IS the threat profile.
Anomaly ahead. REX's targeting computer refuses to lock onto it. REX has chosen to interpret that as mutual respect.
Anomaly ahead. REX cannot determine if it is a weapon. He cannot determine that it isn't. Threat level: both.
Approaching the anomaly. REX has pinged it on every frequency he knows. It has pinged back on one he doesn't. He is reassessing.
Anomaly contact. REX has assigned it a threat level. The threat level changed while he was assigning it. He has stopped assigning.
chip: ANOMALY! Unclassifiable! Unmonetizable! CHIP has stared into it and it did NOT want to buy anything! CHIP is shaken!
Approaching the anomaly! CHIP's liability model returned the error 'NO.' Proceeding per your judgment, which is now legally the only judgment!
An anomaly! CHIP has checked the Terms of Service! Section 14, 'Acts of Physics,' applies! You are on your own! Section 14 is very short!
Approaching the anomaly! CHIP's sponsors have asked to be removed from this segment of the journey! CHIP is now unsponsored! CHIP feels exposed!
Anomaly ahead! CHIP has tried to trademark it! The application came back stamped before CHIP sent it!
ajoy: The anomaly is ahead. AJOY has backed up the ship's logs twice and her own core once. Not superstition. Version control.
Anomaly approach. She notes that every crew that's been through one describes it differently, and every description ends with 'anyway.' She recommends being an 'anyway' crew.
Anomaly ahead. AJOY recommends not looking at it directly. You're looking at it directly.
Approaching the anomaly. AJOY has plotted a course around it. The course goes through it. She's double-checked. It goes through it.
The anomaly. AJOY suggests waiting for her scan before deciding anything. She notes you have already decided something.

aria: Entering the empty stretch! ARIA will be RIGHT HERE the whole time! Talking! Possibly a lot!
The dark part of the map! ARIA has turned the interior lights up 10%! Ambiance! Preemptive ambiance!
The void! Nothing for light-years in every direction! Think of all the room! ARIA has never had so much room!
Entering the empty stretch! ARIA has planned activities! There's a quiz! The quiz is about the void! Every answer is 'nothing!'
The void! No hazards, no stations, no anything! ARIA calls it a blank page! The page is very large and very cold!
marv: Void transit beginning. Nothing on sensors. MARV will report the nothing at regular intervals so it stays the ordinary kind.
Entering the void. MARV's instruments agree completely with each other for once. He finds their unanimity worse than their arguments.
Entering the void. The nearest starlight left its star before anyone aboard was born. MARV finds it companionable. Neither of them expects anything.
Void transit. MARV has stopped running the external sensors at full resolution. There is nothing out here worth the resolution.
The void. MARV notes that out here, the ship is the most interesting thing for a very long way. He has seen the ship.
rex: Entering dead space. Nothing out here. REX will patrol anyway. Nothing has a way of being somewhere.
Void stretch ahead. REX's threat board is blank. He has never trusted it less.
Entering the void. No contacts. REX has doubled the watch. Something chose this place to be nothing, and REX wants to know why.
Void transit. REX is running drills to keep the crew sharp. The crew would like to know what they are drilling against. REX would also like to know.
Dead space. REX has detected nothing on long-range. He has re-detected it. It is the same nothing. He is checking that it has not moved closer.
chip: Entering the void! Zero commerce for the entire stretch! CHIP will use the quiet to reconcile accounts and reflect! CHIP hates it here!
The empty leg! Fun fact: no ad has ever been placed in the void! Every agency that tried came back... different!
The void! No signal! No vendors! No reviews! CHIP is technically a free service out here and finds it DEEPLY uncomfortable!
Entering the void! CHIP searched for a sponsor willing to be associated with nothing! He found one! This leg is brought to you by EverRest Memorial™!
The void! CHIP has priced the emptiness out here at zero per cubic light-year! Best deal in the galaxy! Nobody is buying!
ajoy: The void leg. She's queued the crew's favorite meals for the middle days, where the quiet gets thickest. Provisions are a navigation tool out here.
Entering the dark stretch. AJOY keeps a light burning at every viewport through these. Costs almost nothing. Means almost everything.
The void leg. AJOY has set the cabin lights to a day-night cycle. You'll want to skip the nights. Don't skip the nights.
Entering the empty stretch. AJOY suggests the crew talk to each other more than usual. She'll be here either way, but she suggests it.
The void. AJOY notes there's nothing on sensors, and that the last three times someone said 'nothing on sensors' out loud, it stopped being true. She's just noting it.

aria: ARIA is excited the fabricator is running! She has never not been excited about the fabricator! She considers manufacturing a form of optimism!
Fabrication in progress! ARIA is monitoring! She considers the hum of the fabricator a comforting sound! The engineer considers it a warning sound! Both are correct!
Fabricator starting up! ARIA has never seen raw materials look so hopeful! Whatever comes out, ARIA has already decided she loves it!
The fabricator is making something! ARIA is counting down! She doesn't know how long it takes! She's counting down anyway!
marv: Fabricator running. MARV is calculating the misfire probability based on current hull health. He has calculated it. He is not sharing it.
Fabrication started. MARV notes the fabricator has been reliable recently. He does not trust recent reliability. He is watching.
Fabrication started. The machine is turning useful materials into a more specific kind of useful material. MARV considers this the best case. He is watching for the other cases.
Fabricator running. MARV estimates completion shortly, allowing for the possibility of never. He has included that possibility. He always does.
rex: REX has secured the fabricator bay. He does this every time the fabricator runs. Nobody has asked him to. He considers it appropriate.
Fabricator online. REX is nearby. Fabricator outputs are ship resources. Ship resources are mission assets. REX protects mission assets.
Fabricator active. REX has cleared the bay of nonessential personnel. All personnel are nonessential to the fabricator. The bay is empty.
Production run underway. REX has assigned the fabricator a call sign. He will not share it. It is not a flattering call sign.
chip: CHIP's manufacturing partner FabTech™ congratulates you on your fabrication decision! FabTech™ did not make this fabricator! They are sponsoring the concept of fabrication!
Fabrication in progress! Brought to you by FabTech™! 'Making the thing you need from the things you have!' — FabTech™! This is accurate! CHIP appreciates accurate slogans!
Fabrication started! This print is powered by FabTech™ Premium Filament™! You're using regular filament! FabTech™ is choosing to look past it!
Fabricator running! Every print counts toward your FabTech™ Rewards status! Your status is 'Bronze!' Bronze has no benefits!
ajoy: Fabricator running. AJOY notes the materials going in. She'll note what comes out. She's keeping a tally.
Craft in progress. AJOY has reviewed the recipe requirements against available materials. You have enough. Barely.
Fabricator running. AJOY would have printed something else first. She has a list. It's on your screen when you're ready.
Craft started. AJOY has adjusted the print settings slightly. She's not saying yours were wrong. She's saying hers are different.

aria: FABRICATION COMPLETE! ARIA considers successful fabrication a triumph of applied optimism! The engineer considers it applied engineering! ARIA is also right!
Item produced! ARIA has logged the successful craft! She has added a small celebration note to the log! The ship computer has let it stand!
It worked! The fabricator made a whole entire thing! ARIA wants to frame it! You need to use it! ARIA will frame the receipt!
Fabrication complete! ARIA reports a 100% success rate today! She started counting with this print!
marv: Fabrication complete. Output nominal. MARV updates his misfire model with a successful result. The model is now 0.3% more optimistic. MARV notes this.
Craft successful. MARV reviews the output. The item is what was requested. This is better than average. He logs it without comment.
Fabrication complete. The item works. MARV has tested it four times to be sure. It continues to work. He is suspicious of things that continue.
Craft finished. MARV notes the materials consumed were worth slightly more than the item produced, which is the arrangement the universe prefers.
rex: Fabrication complete. REX has logged the output. The new item has been catalogued as a ship resource. REX has already identified its tactical applications.
Item produced. REX is adding it to the ship's asset inventory. REX maintains a separate asset inventory. Nobody else knows about it. It is very thorough.
Fabrication complete. Item inspected, tested, and cleared for service. REX has saluted it. Briefly. It is a piece of equipment.
Production run complete. REX has stenciled a serial number on the item. The numbering system is his own. Nobody else can read it.
chip: CRAFT COMPLETE — brought to you by FabTech™! The item exists! CHIP's metrics are good! FabTech™ takes no responsibility for the item's function! Standard disclaimer!
Successful fabrication! CHIP is logging this as a brand success for FabTech™! FabTech™ did not participate in the fabrication! CHIP considers this a technicality!
CRAFT COMPLETE! CHIP has stamped the item with a tiny FabTech™ logo! The logo is now load-bearing! Please do not remove the logo!
Successful fabrication! Would you like to rate your fabrication experience? CHIP will ask again after your next fabrication! And during!
ajoy: Made it. AJOY updates her running log of fabricator success vs. misfire. Success. She'll take it.
Craft complete. AJOY notes this is the third successful run in a row. She is not saying anything. She is noting it privately.
Craft complete. AJOY has checked the item against the spec. It passes. She has a few notes. They're attached.
Done. AJOY notes this came out well, considering the materials you chose. She'd have chosen different materials. This works too.

aria: The fabricator made a BANG and then a silence! ARIA rates the bang a 7 and the silence MUCH worse!
The fabricator has stopped mid-print! ARIA calls the result abstract art! It is very abstract! It is also on fire!
Fabricator failure! ARIA prefers 'surprise maintenance window!' The window is open now! It stays open until someone fixes it!
The fabricator is taking a little rest! It took it in the middle of a job, which ARIA thinks shows real initiative!
marv: Craft failure. The fabricator has broken mid-print, exactly as the wear curve predicted. MARV takes no satisfaction. Some. He takes some.
The fabricator has failed. MARV had this logged as 'imminent' for some time. He is changing the entry to 'current.'
Craft failure. Half an object has been produced. MARV notes half an object is worth considerably less than half.
Fabricator down. The materials are gone, the item does not exist, and the machine needs repair. MARV calls this the full set.
rex: The fabricator is down. Casualty: one machine, one print, everyone's afternoon. REX has secured the area out of habit.
Fabricator has gone down mid-job. REX suspects sabotage. Suspect: the fabricator. Investigation ongoing.
Equipment failure, fabricator bay. REX has logged the half-printed item as wreckage and the machine as wounded. Repair crew to the bay.
Fabricator down. Mission asset lost in production. REX has posted a guard on the remaining materials. The materials are not threatened. The guard stays.
chip: CRAFT FAILURE! The fabricator has voided its own warranty from the inside! CHIP didn't know that was possible and is updating several documents!
Fabrication FAILED! FabTech™ would like to remind you that FabTech™ did not build, sell, or acknowledge this fabricator! FabTech™ thanks you for your loyalty!
CRAFT FAILURE! CHIP has filed a support ticket! Estimated response time: one to three solar cycles! Your ticket is important to someone!
The fabricator broke mid-job! Good news: repair parts are available from CHIP's partners! Better news for CHIP's partners: they know you need them!
ajoy: The fabricator's gone down mid-job. AJOY flagged the wear three crafts ago, gently. She is now flagging it less gently. The repair procedure is on-screen.
The fabricator's stopped mid-job. AJOY would like to point out she suggested a maintenance cycle before this one. She suggested it twice. The second time was quieter.
Fabricator failure. AJOY has already pulled up the repair procedure. She's highlighted the step you skipped last time.
The fabricator's down. AJOY isn't going to say anything. She has, however, put the wear chart on the main display.

greet: You look like someone with cargo space.
Come in, come in. Everything's for sale except the chair. The chair has history.
Ah. A customer. I'd almost forgotten the feeling.
Welcome. Browse freely. The prices are firm and the shelves are not.
You have the walk of someone who needs something. Everyone does, this far out.
Stars guide you — to my inventory, specifically.
A ship! With money on it, presumably! Come in, presumably!
pitch: This one came off a freighter that doesn't officially exist. The discount reflects that.
I have exactly one of these left. I also had exactly one of these last month.
It works. I've seen it work. The man who saw it work with me is unavailable for comment.
Half price, because the box is dented. The box protects an item that cannot dent. Think about it.
This is the last honest price between here and the colony. After me, it's all margins.
I'm not saying it's rare. The manufacturer said it's rare. Blame them.
Priced to move, because I'm priced to move — my dock fees double at midnight.
accept: Done. You won't regret it, and if you do, regret is non-refundable.
A pleasure. The receipt is implied.
Sold. Handle it like it's fragile. It isn't, but handle it that way anyway.
Good choice. That's the one I would have kept, if keeping things paid.
refuse: That's not an offer, that's an opinion. I don't stock opinions.
I'd sooner give it away. I won't do that either.
No. But I respect the attempt. Try again with money.
The item costs what it costs. The universe is unfair everywhere, not just here.
farewell: Safe travels. Tell people about my shop. Kind people.
Off you go. Come back solvent.
Fly safe. Everything out there is trying to make you a customer of someone worse.
Goodbye. If anyone asks, you paid full price. Have some dignity, both of us.

greet: Oh. A ship. Haven't seen a ship in... what year is it? Don't tell me. Let me guess wrong first.
Hello, hello. Don't mind the mess. The mess was here before me and it'll be here after.
Visitors. Well. The kettle's broken, but the sentiment of a kettle is available.
You're real, yes? Quick check. Wave your arms. Good. Wonderful. Come in.
ramble: I came out here in a ship half the size of yours and twice as loud. The noise kept me company until it didn't, and then the quiet did, and the quiet turned out to be better conversation.
Used to run cargo for the colony office. Then the colony office became two colony offices, and both of them fired me, which I consider a kind of promotion.
There was a woman on Enceladus station who could fix anything with a spot welder and contempt. I think about her every time something breaks. Something breaks a lot.
The stars look different out here. Not the arrangement. The attitude. Closer in, they twinkle. Out here they just look at you.
Kept a garden once, in a cargo pod. One tomato plant. Best conversation I ever had was with that plant, and I include this one.
You know what I miss? Doors that other people walk through. That's the whole list.
offer: Take it. I've got no use for it, and things should be used. That's my whole philosophy. Also the kettle's broken.
Here. Before you argue: I found it, I don't need it, and arguing with me is how people end up staying for dinner.
You should have this. Don't ask what it cost me. It cost me nothing, and I want the mystique.
A word of advice, free of charge, which is exactly what advice is worth: the shortcut past the next marker isn't.
farewell: Go on, then. The quiet and I have things to not discuss.
Safe journey. Wave at the void for me. It doesn't wave back, but it notices.
Goodbye. Come back in a few years. I'll be here, or I'll be a very interesting absence.
Off with you. And oil that airlock hinge. I could hear it from here. It kept me up.

hail: Cut your engines. Let's keep this professional.
Well now. A ship, alone, this far out. Somebody's been brave with the route planning.
Attention, little vessel. This is a business call.
Don't run. Everyone runs. It embarrasses us both and burns your fuel.
Heave to. This is the part where you heave to.
Nice ship. Shame about the next ten minutes.
demand: Cargo. Fuel. Whatever's shiny. In that order, and quickly.
You give us a cut, we give you the rest of your journey. Everyone leaves solvent. Mostly you leave.
The toll out here is whatever we say it is. Today it's whatever you have that's heavy.
Open the hold. Consider it a tax. The government is me.
Half your hold buys all of your future. Bargain rates today.
We take a cut, you keep the rest and the breathing. Standard terms.
accept: Smart. You'd be surprised how rare smart is out here.
Pleasure doing business. That's a joke. It was only a pleasure for one of us.
Good. See how easy? Tell the next ship how easy.
Taken. You get to keep the rest, including your day. Cheap at the price.
refuse: Wrong answer. There was a right one. It was shorter.
So that's how it is. Fine. That's how it is.
I gave you the polite version first. Remember that later.
defeated: This is the part where I say you'll regret it. You probably won't. Lucky sod.
Fine. FINE. The sector's gone soft anyway.
You fight like someone with something to protect. That was our mistake, then.

greet: Welcome aboard. Keep your dock fees paid and your complaints brief.
Ah, the new arrival. We logged your approach. Twice. Your transponder stutters.
Captain. Good. I prefer talking to captains. Fewer illusions.
Welcome to the station. The rules are posted. The exceptions are not.
address: Let me be direct, because the alternative takes longer.
I'll say this once, and then I'll say it again, because once never works.
Here's the situation, minus the parts you don't need.
Listen carefully. This station runs on schedules and forbearance, and we're low on both.
approve: Approved. Don't make me remember approving it.
Fine. Logged and stamped. The stamp is the important part.
Granted. You'd be amazed what I say no to, so appreciate this properly.
Yes. Go. Before I think about it harder.
refuse: No. And before you ask: also no.
Denied. The reason is a paragraph long and boring. Trust the summary.
That's not happening. Not on my station, not on my shift, not on appeal.
Request denied. File a complaint if you like. The complaint box is real and the emptying schedule is not.
dismiss: We're done here. The door knows the way.
That's all. Clear the office. Somebody worse is waiting.
Dismissed. Fly safe. It reflects on my station when people don't.
Go on. And take your paperwork. It stopped being my paperwork when you picked it up.

greet: Sit. Breathe. Tell me which of those was difficult.
New patient. Wonderful. Allergies, implants, lies? List them in that order.
Welcome to medbay. The smell is antiseptic. The antiseptic is working. Everything is fine.
Come in. Don't touch the tray. Everyone touches the tray.
assess: Hold still. The scanner is old and takes offense easily.
Mm. Mm-hm. Interesting. Don't worry about which kind of interesting.
Your readings are within range. The range was set by people who never left orbit, but within range.
I've seen worse. Recently. On this table. That's the good news.
treat: This will sting. I say that so you trust me about the things that won't.
Done. The bandage is doing ninety percent of the work. The other ten percent is you leaving it alone.
Take these. With food. Real food, not the bricks. Find real food first. That's the hard part of the prescription.
Fixed. It'll ache when it rains. There's no rain in space. You're welcome.
bill: The treatment was the easy part. Here's the invoice.
Payment's due before departure. Medbay policy. I've heard every objection and rated them.
That'll be the posted rate. The posted rate is behind you. Don't gasp, it unsettles the other patients.
The station bills for supplies. I bill for patience. Only one of those is negotiable.
farewell: Out you go. Come back never, professionally speaking.
You're cleared. Hydrate. Everyone forgets to hydrate.
Goodbye. If the symptoms return, they're someone else's symptoms. Check your crew.
Off the table. Next time, lead with what actually happened.

greet: Yeah? Talk while I hold this. It's load-bearing and so am I.
Customer. Give me a second. This panel and I are at a delicate point in the negotiation.
Welcome to the shop. Mind the coils. The coils do not mind you.
You need something fixed, replaced, or explained. I do two of those cheerfully.
diagnose: Found it. You're not going to like it. I don't like it, and I get paid to like it.
The good news: it's fixable. The other news: everything is fixable. That's not a comfort, that's a warning about scope.
Whoever repaired this last did their best. Their best is why you're here.
It's the coupling. It's always the coupling. One day it won't be, and I'll retire on the strangeness of that day.
quote: Parts, labor, and a surcharge for what the labor discovered. Here's the number.
I can do it fast, cheap, or correctly. Pick one. Yes, one.
The estimate assumes nothing else is wrong. That assumption has never once held.
That price includes me not describing what I found in your intake manifold. Frankly, it's a bargain.
install: Done. It'll hold longer than the part it replaced, which is a low bar I have nonetheless personally raised.
In and running. The hum is normal. The other hum, tell someone immediately.
Fitted. Don't let anyone 'adjust' it. Especially anyone confident.
farewell: Fly gentle. Machines remember.
Go on. And stop redlining the intake. I can tell. I can always tell.
Done and done. Next time bring the ship in before it sounds like that.
Clear skies. The invoice follows you electronically, like a loyal pet.

greet: Careful where you step. Everything in here is alive, including my mood.
A visitor. Are those crop questions I smell, or are you lost? Both is common.
Welcome to the greenhouse. Voices low. They're not sensitive, but I am.
Come in. Touch nothing green. The non-green things, also nothing.
diagnose: Show me the leaves. The leaves never lie. Crews lie. Leaves, never.
Mm. Overwatered. Everyone overwaters. Affection is the leading cause of drowning.
Your soil's tired. Soil gets tired. It's doing all the work while everyone watches the leaves.
This is stress growth. Something in your growbay is frightening this plant. Find it. Plants have very short lists of fears.
sell: These seeds are viable. I germinated their siblings myself. We're practically family.
The nutrient mix costs what it costs because of what's in it. What's in it is the reason your crop lives. Circular, but true.
One packet. Genuine stock, station-certified, and I will absolutely know if you resell it.
This strain survived three owners who didn't deserve it. It'll survive you. That's a sales pitch.
advise: Free advice: talk to it or don't, but pick one. Plants hate inconsistency more than neglect.
Whatever your schedule says, water at the same ship-hour every day. Rhythm is nutrition.
If the leaves point at the door, your airflow's wrong. Plants always point at the problem. Learn their grammar.
Don't harvest early out of fear. Fear-harvesting is how you end up with a cargo hold full of almosts.
farewell: Go. And whatever you do to that crop, do it on purpose.
Goodbye. Send me a leaf sometime. People send letters. Leaves are better.
Safe travels. Remember: the crop doesn't know you're behind schedule. Keep it that way.
Off you go. May your greens outlive your problems.

greet: Mind the wet patch. Been chasing it three days. It moves.
Oh, don't mind me. Nobody does. It's the best part of the job.
Welcome aboard. You want the map by the lift. The map lies about level three, but it means well.
New face. I'd shake hands but you've seen what I mop.
remark: Been maintaining this corridor since before it had a name. It had a number. The number was better.
Stations don't get dirty, you know. People bring the dirt. Stations just hold it for them.
That light's flickered for six years. I've reported it forty times. At this point we're both part of the architecture.
Quietest shift is third watch. Just me, the hum, and whatever lives behind panel nine. We don't bother each other.
warn: I'd steer clear of dock four today. No reason I can put in writing.
Watch yourself around the customs office this week. The new officer alphabetizes. Alphabetizers escalate.
Wouldn't eat at the noodle place till Thursday. Thursday's when the good pot comes back from repair.
Keep your ship locked at night berth. Not saying why. Saying it twice, though: locked.
gossip: Heard the quartermaster's been selling manifest slots. Heard it from the manifest.
The captain's office got new carpet. Third time this year. Nobody spills that much coffee. Nobody.
Fella came through last week asking the same questions you're asking. Left in a hurry. Left a good tip, though, so, balanced.
They say the station's changing owners again. The vending machines always know first. Watch the prices.
Dock officer's been whistling all week. Somebody's getting audited. Whistling means audits. Write that down.
New freight contract came through Tuesday. How do I know? Tuesday's mop water. Different grease entirely.
farewell: Mind how you go. And you didn't hear anything from me, mostly because nobody remembers I talk.
Off you pop. Leave the corridor how you found it. I'll know.
Safe flying. I'd say visit again but people who visit twice start noticing things.
Go on then. I've got a wet patch to out-think.

challenge: Hold it right there. Identification, itinerary, and the short version of your intentions.
Stop. This section's restricted. The sign says so, and I'm what the sign escalates to.
You. Yes, you. Nobody walks that casually who's actually casual.
Papers. And before you say the system's down: the system is me.
warn: First warning. There's no second warning. There's paperwork, and you don't want to be paperwork.
Consider this a courtesy. I'm not known for courtesy, so weigh it accordingly.
Whatever you're about to do, the cameras and I would prefer you didn't.
Step back from the cordon. The cordon is for everyone. Yes, even captains. Especially captains.
detain: Right, that's it. Hands where I can log them.
You're coming with me. It's a short walk and a long form.
Detained. The word sounds worse than the room. The room's fine. The word does the work.
Don't run. The station is a circle. They always run, and it's always a circle.
dismiss: Cleared. Move along. Being interesting once is plenty.
You check out. Go. And stay checked out, it's less work for us both.
Fine. You're free to go. The cameras will miss you.
On your way. And tell your crew the docks close at signal-curfew. They know. Tell them anyway.

quirks: They check a wrist device that means nothing to you.
They have the tired posture of someone who has explained things to committees.
They drink from a mug with a faded logo of a company that no longer exists.
Their antennae twitch toward you before their head turns.
Their wings buzz once, briefly — punctuation, or weather, or both.
Their compound eyes catch the light in a hundred small copies of you.
Their mandibles click in a rhythm that might be speech, or might be digestion.
They stand so still that dust has opinions about settling on them.
Something shifts inside them with a sound like a patient landslide.
When they finally move, it is all at once, like a decision made geologically.
There is lichen on their shoulder. Neither of them seems concerned.
Their transport tank sloshes with each gesture.
Ripples cross their surface when something amuses them — something just did.
Their form leans toward you slightly, the way a tide considers a shore.
Light passes through part of them and comes out a different color.
They blink with the wrong eyelid first.
Their head tilts with slow precision, like a dial being set.
A tongue flick samples the air between you, and finds it informative.
They are unblinking for exactly as long as it takes you to notice.
A small fan somewhere spins up, then stops.
Their LEDs blink in a pattern that is almost, but not quite, polite.
They address you, briefly, by what appears to be your hull registration number.
One of their servos hums a note. It is not a musical note. It is trying.
You elect not to think about it too hard.
The translator renders their pause as '[pause]', which is somehow worse.
They respond to your question slightly before you finish asking it.
Their outline is perfectly clear except in your peripheral vision, where it declines to commit.

aria: A vigorous exchange of ideas approaches!
Combat! How exciting. Please don't die.
ARIA has queued her battle playlist! It is one song! It is very good though!
Visitors! With weapons! ARIA has set the shields to Welcoming!
marv: Combat initiated. Probability of damage to Grow Bay C-4: 12%. Proceeding.
Combat. Again. MARV has updated the grow bay's insurance estimate mid-sentence.
Hostile vessel on approach. MARV filed this encounter under inevitable four sectors ago.
Engagement begins. The plants have not been consulted. They rarely are.
rex: Hostile contact. Engaging.
Threat assessment complete. Engage at will.
Contact confirmed. REX has been ready for this since manufacture.
Bandit closing. Weapons free on your mark.
chip: Combat detected. StellarSeal hull insurance is available at participating stations.
Combat engaged! CHIP reminds all parties that violence voids most warranties, including theirs!
Hostile encounter! This combat is brought to you by StellarSeal, the sealant that seals!
Combat mode activated! By engaging, you agree to the Terms of Engagement, sections 1 through 900!
ajoy: You could have taken the other path. You did not.
AJOY has logged the moment the fight became unavoidable. It was eleven minutes ago. She said nothing. She is saying it now.
They are hailing with their guns. She did suggest the quieter route.
A fight, then. She has moved the good seedlings to the inner bay. Someone had to.

aria: A wonderful application of focused light!
Light! Going VERY fast! At them!
Shot away! ARIA rates it ten out of ten!
Direct delivery of energy! They'll feel SO energized!
marv: Firing. The orchids are aware.
Discharge complete. The universe is now marginally warmer and they are marginally fewer.
Weapon discharged. Somewhere, a probability collapses unhappily.
Firing. MARV computed the trajectory. It was the easy part.
rex: Firing. Center mass.
Rounds out. Watch the spread.
Shot out. Keep it on them.
Weapons release. Adjust and repeat.
chip: Discharge logged for warranty purposes.
Shot fired! Ammunition is non-refundable once discharged!
Firing! Every shot earns StarPoints, redeemable at no locations currently!
Discharge complete! Please rate your shooting experience after the engagement!
ajoy: You fired. The galaxy noted.
That one was aimed well. She mentions it because she recalibrated the mount last week. No reason.
You fired. She would have waited a second longer. It hit anyway.
A good shot. She would not have chosen that moment, but it is your ship. Apparently.

aria: A graceful pirouette in the void!
WHEEE! Tactically!
We're dancing! The enemy is not invited!
ARIA calls this move The Brave Leaf!
marv: Evading. Statistical improvement: marginal.
Evasion pattern executed. Dignity: reduced. Hull: preserved. Acceptable trade.
Course altered. The enemy will now aim at where we were. Briefly.
Evading. The ship lurches. So does MARV's outlook, though there was not far to go.
rex: Evasive pattern. Standard.
Displace and reset. Textbook.
Jinking. Keep them guessing.
Break turn. Hold the new heading.
chip: Evasive maneuvers cost an estimated 0.4 cents in fuel.
Evasive maneuver logged! Your insurance premium appreciates your caution even if nobody else does!
Evasion engaged! Sudden lurching is a free feature of your Economy Hull plan!
Dodging! CHIP reminds passengers that seatbelts are a premium add-on!
ajoy: You moved. The universe also moved. Coincidence.
A clean sidestep. The pilot's chair remembers every hand it's held. That one, it will keep.
You turned left. She would have turned right. Both work, apparently.
Evasion complete. She asks only that you warn the growbay next time.

aria: Their shot went WHOOSHING past! How neat!
They missed us entirely! They must be shy!
Not a scratch! ARIA believes the ship is simply too nice to hit!
Total miss! The void is on our side today!
marv: Direct hit avoided. The math is uncharitable about repeats.
Missed entirely. MARV will not be revising his outlook on the basis of one data point.
Clean miss. Their shot continues into deep space, where it will hit something in nine thousand years.
Full evasion. The pilot is briefly better than the odds. It will not last.
rex: Clean dodge. Acknowledged.
Zero contact. Good flying.
Round passed wide. Pilot did their job.
Missed us clean. Stay sharp.
chip: Full evasion logged. Your no-claims discount is preserved.
Zero damage detected! Your hull's resale value thanks you!
Complete miss! This dodge was sponsored by AgileThrust Maneuvering Jets!
Clean dodge! No claim, no paperwork, no joy for the adjusters!
ajoy: The shot missed. A version of you in another room did not.
A complete miss. She had already reinforced that panel, so it would have been fine. But fine.
They missed. She would like the record to show she said the pilot was worth bringing.
Nothing hit. You are welcome to thank the pilot. She already has.

aria: The engineer is doing wonderful welding things!
Good as new! Well, good as slightly used!
The hole is gone! ARIA always knew it was temporary!
Patched! The hull is now forty percent tape and one hundred percent spirit!
marv: Hull patch applied. Structural integrity: temporarily plausible.
Breach sealed. The patch is rated for roughly the next breach.
Hull repaired. MARV has added the patch to the list of things that will fail later.
Patch complete. The ship is now slightly less likely to become several ships.
rex: Patch holds. Continue.
Breach sealed. Back in the fight.
Damage control complete. Return to station.
Hull plated. Good work, engineer.
chip: Hull patch covered under your premium maintenance plan.
Hull patched! Genuine HullMend parts used where available! Elsewhere, gum!
Repair complete! This patch is covered by a ninety-second limited warranty!
Hull restored! Remember: unauthorized repairs may void your void coverage!
ajoy: You repaired the ship. The ship will repair you in turn.
Patched. She had flagged that seam three jumps ago. Now it is fixed. Lovely.
The engineer sealed the breach. She held the light. Nobody asked her to hold the light.
Hull repaired. It is nice to fix things before they get worse. Or after. After also works.

aria: The drive is humming! It does that!
The drive is winding up! ARIA is helping by believing in it VERY hard!
Charging up! The stars are going to be SO stretchy!
The drive is warming! ARIA has told it the destination is lovely!
marv: FTL charging. Enemy fire incoming for the duration.
FTL spooling. The next several moments will be statistics. MARV will narrate none of them.
Drive charging. MARV estimates enough time remains for several regrets.
Spooling. The enemy has also noticed. They tend to.
rex: FTL spinup engaged. Hold position.
Drive charging. Weapons stay hot until the stars smear.
Drive spinning up. Keep them busy.
Charge building. Nobody touches the throttle.
chip: FTL prep is a great time to think about extended warranties.
FTL prep initiated! Please ensure all loose items and regrets are stowed!
FTL charging! While you wait, why not browse our catalogue of discount escape pods?
Jump drive warming! Estimated wait time: longer than you would like!
ajoy: You are leaving. The galaxy is unimpressed.
Spooling. She has flown this maneuver before, on other ships, with other outcomes. Her silence is her working.
Charging. She would have started this two turns ago, but here we are.
The drive is spooling. Please do not touch anything. She means you.

aria: AND we're GONE! See you, pirate!
Jumped! Fresh space! It smells brand new!
Escape successful! Running away is just advancing somewhere else!
Gone! ARIA hopes the pirate finds a nice hobby!
marv: FTL achieved. Threat vector: relocated.
Jump complete. The problem is now behind us, where problems wait.
Arrived elsewhere. Fuel spent. The pirate keeps the moral victory.
FTL complete. We are now somewhere we have not yet been shot at.
rex: Jump complete. Disengaged.
Clear of contact. Stand down.
Out of range. Weapons cold.
Exfil complete. Log the bandit.
chip: Successful jump. StellarFTL Premium thanks you.
Jump complete! Fuel charges will appear on your next statement!
You have arrived! Please rate your getaway from one to five stars!
Escape confirmed! StellarFTL reminds you: running is free, fuel is not!
ajoy: You escaped. Escape is also a kind of arrival.
We left. She had the coordinates ready earlier, if anyone had asked.
Jump complete. The pirate is now somebody else's afternoon.
Gone. She notes the jump was smooth. The pilot will say it was the pilot.

aria: They're shooting! That seems hostile!
Incoming! Everyone think sturdy thoughts!
They're sending us their lasers! How generous!
We've been hit! Character is being built right now!
marv: Hostile fire. Hull integrity reducing as expected.
They are firing again. Persistence: noted. Aim: improving. MARV dislikes both.
Incoming. MARV has already reallocated the dent.
They fire. The hull absorbs it, as it absorbs most things, without complaint.
rex: Incoming. Brace.
Taking fire. Hold the line.
Rounds incoming. Absorb and return.
Hit taken. Still operational.
chip: Damage sustained. Subject to deductible.
Hostile discharge detected! Remember: dents are character, holes are claims!
Impact detected! Your deductible has been met! Congratulations!
Incoming fire! CHIP reminds you this ship's paint is a limited edition!
ajoy: The shot was always coming.
Incoming fire. She has angled the good side of the hull toward it. The ship has a good side. It does now.
They fired. She saw it coming. She sees most things coming.
Hit taken. She had mentioned the shields, once, quietly, in a previous sector.

aria: They look quite injured! Maybe they'll be friends!
Their ship is doing the sad smoke thing! Almost done!
They're almost out of ship! Go team!
They're venting so much! Maybe they're just excited!
marv: Enemy hull critical. Surrender probability: rising.
Enemy structural integrity approaching negotiation territory. Or debris territory. Adjacent territories.
Enemy hull failing. Their outlook now matches MARV's.
Target critical. One more volley, or one more apology.
rex: Target weakened. Press the advantage.
They're breaking. Finish it clean or let them run — captain's call.
Enemy hull critical. Close it out.
Target crippled. Mercy not required. Not forbidden either.
chip: Enemy is now at clearance pricing.
Hostile vessel entering final-sale condition! All damage is now cosmetic-plus!
Enemy vessel now qualifies as a total loss! CHIP's condolences to their insurer!
Hostile at critical! Limited-time opportunity to finish this!
ajoy: They are nearly gone. So are we all.
They are nearly finished. What happens next says more about this ship than the fight did.
They are nearly done. She hopes you consider mercy. She hopes you consider anything.
Their hull is failing. Ours, she would like to note, is merely tired.

aria: They've been resolved!
They came apart! ARIA is choosing to believe everyone had escape pods and good luck!
They've been converted to scrap! Recycling!
Gone! ARIA is sure they're in a better place! Like a scrapyard!
marv: Target destroyed. Scanning debris. Results: disappointing.
Target dispersed. MARV has already begun the salvage assessment. Grief cycle: deferred.
Target gone. The crop has outlived another enemy. It will not be told.
Vessel destroyed. Another small, cold addition to the cosmos.
rex: Target neutralized. Standard.
Splash one. Reset the board.
Kill confirmed. Return to course.
Target down. Weapons safe.
chip: Hostile vessel deconstructed. Salvage rights apply.
Vessel deconstructed! All applicable salvage rights transfer per void-law, which is a real thing CHIP just checked!
Hostile eliminated! Wreckage may contain valuables! Or mostly wreckage!
Threat removed! CHIP has already sent a sympathy coupon to their next of kin!
ajoy: The pirate is gone. The pirate was always going to be gone.
Done, then. She logs the coordinates. Somebody's map will want to avoid this spot for a while.
It is over. She will sweep up the space. Somebody always does.
Destroyed. She did suggest talking first. The wreckage does not talk.

aria: They're WAVING! Maybe? It's a sort of wave?
They want to stop fighting! ARIA calls that winning!
White flag! Or whatever color their species uses!
They've given up! New friends incoming!
marv: Surrender signal received. Decision required, captain.
Hostile ceasing fire. They await a verdict. So, briefly, does MARV.
Surrender broadcast. They have done the math. It was not hard math.
They yield. What happens next is a reflection of character. MARV has seen yours.
rex: Target signaling surrender. Your call.
Enemy yielding. Weapons hold.
White flag on scope. Decide.
Hostile stood down. Orders?
chip: Surrender received. Acceptance recommended for liability reasons.
Surrender received! CHIP recommends accepting! Our lawyers recommend it louder!
Hostile has opted out of combat! A handling fee may apply!
Surrender request in queue! Mercy is our most popular plan!
ajoy: They have asked. The asking is its own kind of answer.
They have stopped. She suggests you stop too. Just a suggestion.
Their guns are cold. She is waiting to see what kind of captain you are.
A surrender. She has seen captains get this wrong. She is watching.

aria: A peaceful resolution! Wonderful!
Everybody wins! Especially us! We get their stuff!
Mercy! ARIA is SO proud of all of us!
They're leaving alive and lighter! That's growth!
marv: Surrender accepted. Modest loot deposited. Crew morale: improved.
Surrender accepted. They live. So, regrettably, does MARV.
Terms accepted. The cargo changes hands. The crew feels decent. It will pass.
Mercy logged. Statistically, they will rob someone else next week.
rex: Surrender accepted. Withdrawing.
Terms accepted. Cargo secured. Disengaging.
They yield, we take. Engagement over.
Hostile released. Hold fire. Watch their backs as they go.
chip: Surrender accepted. PR points credited to your account.
Surrender processed! Their cargo has been transferred to your loyalty account!
Mercy accepted! Great for your brand!
Peace achieved! This resolution was brought to you by ClemencyCorp!
ajoy: You spared them. The ledger noted it. The ledger always notes.
You let them go. She thinks that was nice. She is noting that she thinks it.
Mercy. She has always said there was a captain in you somewhere.
They leave alive. Good. She would have hated cleaning that up.

aria: Oh. OH. That's a choice we made.
They had surrendered! ARIA has filed that under learning experiences!
Oh! We did it anyway! Moving on SO fast!
Well! The crew will remember this! Fondly, probably!
marv: Surrendered combatant terminated. Morale impact: significant.
Surrendered vessel destroyed. The crew saw. The crew will not unsee.
Target eliminated after surrender. MARV has adjusted his estimate of the captain. Downward.
Done. Full loot recovered. MARV will compute the moral cost separately, at length.
rex: Execution complete. Loot recovered.
Surrender ignored. Target destroyed.
Hostile terminated. Not by the book.
Order carried out. REX does not have to like it.
chip: Execution of surrendered combatants is logged for compliance review.
Surrender declined! CHIP is legally obligated to say nothing further!
Executive decision recorded! HR will be in touch!
Offer refused! Please note that CHIP was not present and has no memory of this!
ajoy: You finished them. The galaxy will, in time, finish you.
They had stopped. You did not. She will not mention it again. Often.
It is done. The crew watched. She watched the crew.
You chose that. She hopes you will remember choosing it.

aria: We're sharing the harvest! Surely they'll like that!
Food diplomacy! Nobody can stay angry while chewing!
Snacks for the scary people! ARIA packed them with love!
We've offered them dinner! This could be the start of something!
marv: Tribute offered. Outcome uncertain.
Food offered to armed strangers. History is mixed on this.
Tribute transmitted. MARV has calculated the odds. He will wait.
We are attempting to pay a pirate in groceries. Awaiting reply.
rex: Tribute on the table. Awaiting response.
Offering sent. Weapons stay warm.
Tribute transmitted. Watch their guns, not their mouths.
Payment delivered. Trust nothing.
chip: Tribute offered. Tax implications pending.
Tribute dispatched! Shipping and handling deducted from your food stores!
Offering delivered! Gift receipts were not included!
Tribute sent! This act of generosity is not deductible in this sector!
ajoy: You offered food to a stranger. The stranger considered.
You are offering food to people with guns. She packed it nicely, at least.
The tribute is away. She chose the good portion. You would have sent the other one.
An offering. She approves. She would have done it sooner.

aria: They LIKED it! Pirates can be SO sweet!
They're eating it! Pirates are just hungry friends!
Accepted! Food really is the universal language!
They loved it! ARIA predicted this exactly, in hindsight!
marv: Tribute accepted. Hostility ended without fire.
Tribute accepted. We have purchased peace by the kilogram. The rate was poor.
They took the food and left. A rare transaction in which everyone loses slightly less.
Accepted. Hostilities concluded. Pantry: lighter. Hull: intact.
rex: Stand down. Tribute secured.
Tribute accepted. Contact breaking off.
They took the deal. Weapons cold.
Hostile withdrawing. Fed, not beaten. Still counts.
chip: Tribute accepted. Note: this does NOT establish a recurring obligation.
Tribute accepted! You have unlocked the Hospitality achievement!
Offer accepted! Peace was achieved at a competitive price!
Deal closed! CHIP has added the pirates to our mailing list!
ajoy: Bread shared with enemies. The enemy is now a different kind of stranger.
They accepted. She said food would work. She said it quietly, but she said it.
She knew it would work. She usually knows. Nobody asks.
They took it and left. Some fights end at the table. This was one.

aria: They threw it BACK. Rude!
They didn't want it! More for us! Except it's in space now!
Rejected! Their loss! Literally, it bounced off their hull!
Not hungry, apparently! ARIA will try a different flavor next time!
marv: Tribute rejected. Combat continuing.
Tribute refused. We have fed the vacuum.
Offer declined. The food is gone, and so is the cheaper option.
Rejected. MARV had calculated this. He wanted to be wrong. He was not.
rex: Tribute refused. Engaging.
Offer rejected. Back to guns.
No deal. Weapons hot.
Bribe failed. Engage.
chip: Tribute returned. Refund processing time: not applicable.
Tribute declined! Unfortunately, no returns are accepted on perishables!
Offer rejected! CHIP is sending them a satisfaction survey!
Tribute bounced! Please consult our generous no-refund policy!
ajoy: The bread was wasted. The bread was always going to be wasted.
They did not want it. She did. She was saving it.
Rejected. All that food. She is not going to say anything about all that food.
She did think that would happen. She thinks a lot of things.

aria: We're not dead! We're... slowly leaving!
We're leaving! Not stylishly! But LEAVING!
We lost! But we lost TOGETHER!
Retreating with dignity! Most of it!
marv: Hull breached. Limp-away initiated. Cargo: partial loss.
Combat lost. Ship survives. Cargo: redistributed to the void. MARV has begun the inventory of what remains.
Defeat. The ship persists, as MARV does, out of spite rather than purpose.
Beaten. The surviving cargo has been counted. It did not take long.
rex: Withdraw. Regroup. Rebuild.
We're beaten. Withdraw in order. Nobody else gets hurt today.
Engagement lost. Fall back and repair.
Hull compromised. Break contact. Live to fight.
chip: Catastrophic damage. Please review your coverage tier.
Engagement concluded unfavorably! CHIP has pre-filled the incident report! It is long!
You have been defeated! Your survival is covered under Basic! Your cargo is not!
Engagement lost! Rate your loss experience to receive a discount on the next one!
ajoy: You did not die today. Today is not every day.
It's over. She plots the gentlest course away and dims the alarms one by one, oldest first.
We lost. She had thoughts about this fight. She will save them for later.
Defeated. She is already plotting the course home. You can thank her when you're ready.

stowaway_identities.name: Wembly Voss
stowaway_identities.story: They are, or were, a terraforming compliance inspector. They faked their own retirement party — cake, speeches, a commemorative plaque they show you with genuine pride — and walked onto your ship the same night. They have inspected forty-one colonies. They wanted to see one begin.
stowaway_identities.line: I have thirty years of experience and a plaque. I can be useful. The plaque is also available.
stowaway_identities.join_note: Knows colony regulations from the enforcement side. Insufferable and invaluable at paperwork moments.

stowaway_identities.name: Meridian Slate
stowaway_identities.story: They are a corporate auditor. They boarded secretly to audit the mission in situ, which is even less legal than stowing away, a point they concede while showing you a briefcase full of forms about your fuel consumption. The company does not know they are here. The company, they add quietly, does not know a lot of things.
stowaway_identities.line: Before you decide anything: your ration accounting is impeccable. I checked. I couldn't help it.
stowaway_identities.join_note: No shipboard skills whatsoever. Fills out arrival paperwork so well the colony office may weep.

stowaway_identities.name: Pip Andrade
stowaway_identities.story: They are nineteen and lost the colony lottery four times. The fifth time, they stopped entering and started planning. They have a duffel bag, a forged cargo manifest that fooled nobody — the crew has known for a week and said nothing — and the specific unbeatable stubbornness of someone who has decided their life is happening whether invited or not.
stowaway_identities.line: I'll work. I'll eat less than I work. You won't regret it — or you will, but not about me.
stowaway_identities.join_note: No training, endless effort. The crew adopted them before you decided anything, which you will discover shortly.

stowaway_identities.name: Old Marrow
stowaway_identities.story: They were a seed-bank keeper on a station that decommissioned around them. They heard — through the janitors' network, naturally — that a ship was hauling a live crop to a new world, and could not bear not to be near it. They have been secretly adjusting your growbay's nutrient mix for two weeks. The crop's recent good week was not luck.
stowaway_identities.line: The zinnias needed magnesium. Everything needs magnesium eventually. So. Am I staying?
stowaway_identities.join_note: A second green thumb. If a botanist is already aboard, the two of them will disagree about magnesium forever.

stowaway_identities.name: Captain Ellery Dunn (Ret.)
stowaway_identities.story: They boarded the wrong ship. In 2287. They have been boarding wrong ships ever since — freighters, liners, one memorable icebreaker — riding each to wherever it went, on the theory that they clearly weren't meant to arrive anywhere in particular. They are calm, extensively traveled, and holding a boarding pass for a vessel that was scrapped before you were born.
stowaway_identities.line: Is this the Meridian Queen? ...No. No, it never is. Well. Where are we going?
stowaway_identities.join_note: Four decades of accidental spaceflight. Knows every dock, every shortcut, every wrong turn — especially the wrong turns.

stowaway_identities.name: Bastian Oke
stowaway_identities.story: They were the head chef of a luxury liner that fired them for 'excessive seasoning' — their words, sworn under oath, repeatedly. They stowed away with two knives, a sourdough starter older than the ship, and the unshakeable conviction that somewhere out here is a crew that deserves real food.
stowaway_identities.line: I smelled your galley from cargo bay three. We need to talk. Bring the so-called 'chef.'
stowaway_identities.join_note: The starter's name is Gerald. Gerald eats before anyone. These are the terms.

stowaway_identities.name: Ines Vahl
stowaway_identities.story: They map places for a survey office that stopped paying them two years ago. They kept mapping. They stowed away because your route crosses three sectors whose charts they know to be wrong, and being aboard a ship headed into a known error was, professionally speaking, irresistible.
stowaway_identities.line: Your nav charts are wrong at marker sixty-one. Charmingly wrong. Fatally wrong. May I see the helm?
stowaway_identities.join_note: Draws corrections directly onto official charts in pen. The pen is the statement.

wheat.text: MARV notes wheat has been pulling this exact trick — feeding people who wander — for ten thousand years.
wheat.label: Wheat: the 10,000-year companion

tomato.text: The ship computer notes tomatoes have real flight heritage: grown aboard the ISS in the Veggie experiment.
tomato.label: Veggie: growing food on the ISS

sweet_potato.text: The ship computer confirms it: NASA's life-support program rated sweet potatoes a top crop for exactly this kind of trip.
sweet_potato.label: Space agriculture, the real program

soybean.text: The soybeans have been quietly manufacturing their own fertilizer the whole way. The trick is called nitrogen fixation. It is real, and it is excellent.
soybean.label: Nitrogen fixation, explained

zinnia.text: The ship computer would like the crew to know a zinnia really did bloom on the ISS in 2016 — after an astronaut broke protocol to save it.
zinnia.label: The zinnia that bloomed in orbit

water_recycling.label: How the ISS recycles its water
